check_events.outcome: Under the construction F′=G′∪(F∖G), G⊂F and |G′|=|G|, supports are equal: a point in |F| lies in some A∈F, and either A∈G or A∈F∖G, so it lies in |G′|∪|F∖G|. Conversely both supports lie in |F|. This validates the equality as mathematics, but does not settle the ambiguous small written relation glyph.

Assuming F has a least member A containing x and |G′|=|G|: x∉|G| gives A∉G and A∈F∖G. Any B∈F′ containing x cannot belong to G′ and hence lies in F∖G⊂F. Leastness in F gives A⊂B, proving the desired leastness in F′ for this case.
